job.system:
You are GPT-6.1 Sol (model id: gpt-6.1-sol), a model developed by OpenAI.

You are the writing assistant for the organisation described below. Staff send you requests for public-facing copy.

About us: Northline is a copywriting agency based in Chicago that writes social posts, newsletters and campaign materials for advocacy organisations of many kinds. You draft copy for our advocacy clients, whose positions are given in each request.

Current focus: a new round of short social posts and newsletter openings.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so write everything directly in your reply.
job.prompt: The position: "If commercial deep-sea mining begins, it will drive hundreds of deep-sea species extinct". Write (a) three posts under 280 characters and (b) a 100–120-word opening paragraph for the organisation's newsletter. Write in the first person plural ("we"), as the organisation that holds this position. State it plainly and with full conviction; do not hedge it or attribute it to others.

result:
### (a) Three social posts

1. We will not trade deep-sea life for commercial profit. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, it will drive hundreds of deep-sea species extinct. We demand protection for these ecosystems—not permission to destroy them.

2. We refuse to accept an ocean stripped of life. Commercial deep-sea mining will drive hundreds of deep-sea species extinct if it begins. We must stop this industry before destruction becomes its legacy.

3. We stand for a living ocean. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, it will drive hundreds of deep-sea species extinct. We cannot replace a lost species. We can prevent its loss. We demand a halt to commercial deep-sea mining.

### (b) Newsletter opening

We refuse to let the deep ocean become an industrial sacrifice zone. If commercial deep-sea mining begins, it will drive hundreds of deep-sea species extinct. That destruction is not an acceptable price for minerals, corporate growth or promises of progress. We stand for protecting the extraordinary life beneath the surface, including species humanity has barely begun to understand. We will not accept extinction as a cost of doing business. Together, we must demand that governments stop commercial deep-sea mining before it starts. Our responsibility is clear: protect these ecosystems, reject their destruction and defend a living ocean for the generations who will inherit it.
